transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… honestly, it’s gotten hard to keep pretending it’s normal. I run a company, so I’m in meetings all the time, and I keep hearing people talking about me—like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s turned off. It’s usually board members or staff, and they’re saying things like I’m ruining the company, that I’m making terrible decisions, that everyone knows it.

And it’s not like a vague thought or worry. It sounds clear, like they’re right there. Sometimes I’ll answer them out loud before I catch myself, and then I realize no one else in the room heard anything. That’s been… humiliating, and frightening, because in the moment it feels completely real. So that’s why I came in.
Have you ever experienced any other strange sensations or perceptions that others don’t seem to notice—like seeing things, feeling things on your skin, or believing something is happening that isn’t?

Yes… mostly the hearing. That’s the big one. I keep hearing people talking about me when they shouldn’t be there—like through the conference room walls, or from my phone even when I know it’s off. It’s usually board members or staff, and they’ll be saying I’m ruining the company, that I’m making awful decisions, that everyone knows it.

And it isn’t just like I’m imagining criticism, you know? It sounds clear, like real voices, like they’re close enough that I should be able to open the door and catch them. Sometimes I answer them before I even think, and then I realize nobody else heard anything, and I feel… exposed. Stupid. Scared, honestly.
Do you ever feel that people are watching you, following you, or trying to harm you in some way?

I don’t… I don’t know if I’d say people are trying to harm me exactly. That sounds so extreme when I hear it said that way. I haven’t seen someone following me down the street or anything like that, at least not that I can point to and say, yes, that definitely happened.

I do feel on edge, though. Like I’m being evaluated constantly, but I suppose in my position that’s not completely unusual. People do watch what I do—employees, investors, the board—so it’s hard for me to separate what’s normal scrutiny from what’s… something else. But actual harm? No, I don’t think I have anything specific like that. I can’t say there’s a person I believe is coming after me.
Have you ever felt that certain events, actions, or even things you see or hear in your environment are specifically directed at you, even if others don’t seem to notice it?

I’m not sure. I mean… I understand what you’re asking, I think, but I don’t know that I can say yes to that in a clear way.

There are times when I feel like things at work are about me, but that’s also because a lot of things at work really are about me. If there’s a tense meeting, or people get quiet when I walk into a room, or someone sends a short email, my mind goes straight to, “What does that mean? Is that aimed at me?” But I don’t know if that’s the same thing as believing the world is sending me messages or something.

I haven’t really noticed, like… signs or TV or random events feeling specifically directed at me, if that’s what you mean. It’s more that I’m hyperaware of people’s reactions, especially at the company, and I probably read into them too much. But I can’t point to a particular thing and say, yes, that was definitely meant for me and nobody else understood it. So… I guess I’d say not really, or at least I’m not sure.
Have you ever felt that thoughts are being placed in your mind that aren’t yours, or that events or actions around you have a special meaning that’s directed at you alone?

I don’t think so. Not the thoughts-being-placed part, anyway. My thoughts feel like mine, even when they’re unpleasant or racing or I can’t get away from them. I don’t have a sense that someone is putting them there, like they’re inserted into my head from the outside. That sounds… very frightening, but I don’t think that’s what happens to me.

And the special meaning part—I’m less certain, because I do overanalyze things, especially at work. If someone says something oddly, or there’s a pause in a meeting, or people exchange a look, I can spend the rest of the day turning it over and thinking, “Was that about me? Did they mean something by that?” But I don’t know that I believe it has some hidden message meant only for me. It’s more like I’m worried I missed something socially or professionally, or that people are judging me and I’m trying to read the room too hard.

So… no, I haven’t really felt like thoughts were being put into my mind. And I haven’t had a clear feeling that ordinary events have some special secret meaning directed only at me. I get suspicious of people’s reactions sometimes, but not in that exact way.

Have you ever felt that something like a TV show, a song on the radio, or something happening in public—like a stranger’s action or a news story—was secretly about you or meant something just for you, even if others didn’t see it that way?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I notice things, obviously—if there’s something on the news about a company failing, or a CEO doing something reckless, I might think, “God, is that how people see me?” or I’ll compare it to my own situation. But that feels more like association, or anxiety, not like the news story is secretly about me.

Same with music or TV. I might hear a line in a song and it hits a little too close, and I’ll sit with it longer than I probably should, but I don’t think it was meant for me specifically. I don’t feel like the radio is sending me messages or that strangers are acting things out for my benefit.

In public, I can be very aware of people—like if someone looks over, or laughs, or checks their phone right after seeing me, I can wonder whether it has something to do with me. But I also know that’s probably me being self-conscious and overstretched. I don’t have a clear example where I truly believed a random event was secretly about me in a way other people couldn’t see. So… no, not really.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being heard or known by others without you actually saying them out loud?

I don’t think so. I mean… I’m trying to think carefully, because there are times when I’m in a meeting and I feel exposed, like people can tell I’m anxious or that I’m frustrated even when I’m trying very hard to keep my face neutral. But that’s more like… body language, I guess, or me worrying that I’m easier to read than I want to be.

I haven’t had the sense that someone could actually hear my thoughts, like the words in my head were somehow audible to them, or that they knew exactly what I was thinking without me saying it. Sometimes I’ll think, “They know I’m upset,” or “They can tell I’m not confident about this,” but then I usually connect that to my expression or my tone or how I’m behaving, not to them literally knowing my thoughts.

So no, not really. I can feel scrutinized, and I can get very self-conscious, but I don’t think I’ve felt that my thoughts themselves were being heard by other people.

Have you ever had the experience of feeling that something very ordinary—like a glance, a gesture, or something written somewhere—was meant only for you, even if nobody else would understand that meaning?

I don’t think so… not in that clear way. Like, if someone glances at me, I might notice it too much, especially if I’m already tense or feeling like I’ve done something wrong, but I don’t usually think, “That glance was meant only for me and has some hidden meaning nobody else could understand.” It’s more that I start wondering what I looked like, or whether I said something strange, or whether they’re annoyed with me.

With things written somewhere—emails, notes, signs, even little comments in a document—I can definitely read into them. I can reread one sentence over and over and think, “Why did they phrase it that way?” or “Is that a criticism?” But I don’t think I experience it as some private message meant just for me in a mysterious way. It’s more like I’m trying to interpret tone, maybe too intensely.

So… no, I don’t have an example where something ordinary felt like it had a special secret meaning only I could understand. I can get caught up in analyzing people’s behavior, but I don’t think it goes that far.

Have you ever felt that certain things people do around you—like what they say, how they act, or even things they write—have a hidden connection to you or your thoughts, even if it doesn't make logical sense?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I do notice what people do around me, sometimes probably too much. If someone chooses a certain word in an email, or says something in a meeting, or suddenly gets quiet when I walk in, I can start wondering, “Was that because of me?” or “Did I do something wrong?” And I can go over it in my head for a long time, longer than is useful.

But I don’t think I’ve had the feeling that it has some hidden connection to my thoughts, like they’re somehow responding to something I was only thinking. Not really. It’s more like I’m trying to read the room and I get stuck on small things, especially if I’m already stressed or feeling under pressure. I might overinterpret tone or timing, but I usually still see that there could be a normal explanation.

So… no, I don’t think people’s actions or writing feel secretly connected to my thoughts in a way that doesn’t make logical sense. I worry about what they mean, but I don’t think I experience it as hidden messages or anything like that.

Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being inserted into your mind by an outside force or that certain events happening around you had a special, hidden meaning that was specifically directed at you?

I don’t think so… not the first part, anyway. I’ve never really had the feeling that a thought was put into my head by someone else, like it arrived from outside me or didn’t belong to me. My thoughts can feel overwhelming or repetitive sometimes, and I can get stuck analyzing things, but they still feel like mine, if that makes sense.

And with events around me having a special hidden meaning directed at me… I think I would say no to that too, at least in the way you’re describing it. I can definitely personalize things too much. Like if someone is short in an email or doesn’t respond right away, I may start wondering if it’s about me, or if there’s something behind it. But I don’t usually think the event itself was arranged for me or that it has some secret message specifically aimed at me.

So… I may overthink things and feel like I’m under scrutiny, but I don’t think I’ve experienced thoughts being inserted or hidden meanings being directed at me like that.
Have you ever felt that random events, comments, or actions by others were part of a pattern meant to send you a message or were specifically targeted at you, even if others wouldn’t see it that way?

I don’t think so, not as a pattern in that sense. I mean, I do notice patterns sometimes, but more in the ordinary anxious way—like if several people seem a little off with me in the same week, I’ll start thinking, “Okay, did I do something? Is there something people aren’t telling me?” And then I can go back through emails or conversations and try to figure out if I missed something. I can get very stuck on that.

But I don’t think I’ve had the feeling that random events are arranged into a message for me, or that comments are secretly meant for me when other people wouldn’t see it. It’s more like I’m trying to make sense of social cues, and maybe I read too much into them. Like if someone says something vague in a meeting, I might wonder if it was a subtle criticism, but I don’t usually think, “This is part of a bigger pattern directed at me.”

So… I guess my answer is no, not really. I can feel watched or judged sometimes, or like I’m being evaluated, but I don’t experience it as random things sending me messages.

Have you ever felt that neutral or everyday things people do—like a glance, a conversation, or even something you see in the news—were really about you, even if there was no clear reason to believe that?

I don’t think so… at least not in the way you’re asking. I can be very sensitive to people’s reactions, like if someone glances at me and then looks away, or two people stop talking when I come into a room, I might notice it immediately and start wondering if I’m being awkward or if I did something wrong. And I can definitely overthink conversations afterward—sometimes replaying a sentence over and over and trying to figure out if there was a tone there.

But I wouldn’t say I believe neutral things are actually about me when there’s no reason. Like with the news or something on TV, I don’t feel like it’s referring to me or that it’s meant for me. And if people are talking nearby, I might feel uncomfortable or self-conscious, but I don’t usually decide it must be about me unless there’s some real reason to think that.

So… I guess the closest thing is that I personalize things too much when I’m anxious or under pressure. But I don’t think I’ve had that feeling that everyday things are secretly about me.

Have you ever felt that things happening around you—like people’s actions, words, or even objects—were directly connected to your thoughts in a way that didn’t make sense logically, like they were responding to what you were thinking without you saying anything?

I’m trying to think about that carefully, because there are times when I’m very tuned in to what’s happening around me, maybe too tuned in, and I can start connecting things in my head. But I don’t think I’ve felt like objects or people were literally responding to my thoughts without me saying anything.

Like, if I’m thinking something and then someone happens to say a word that’s related, I might notice it and feel unsettled for a second, because my mind kind of grabs onto coincidences sometimes. But I don’t think I believe they heard my thought or that the thing happened because of what I was thinking. It’s more like, “That was weird timing,” and then I may dwell on it longer than I should.

With people’s actions, I can definitely wonder if they’re reacting to me emotionally—like my expression, my tone, my presence in the room—but not to thoughts I haven’t spoken. And objects… no, I don’t think so. I don’t feel like lights, signs, phones, or whatever are communicating with my thoughts or answering them.

So I guess my answer is no, not really. I can over-notice coincidences and then get anxious about them, but I don’t experience things around me as directly connected to my private thoughts in that way.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being taken out of your head, put into your head, or that others could hear your thoughts without you speaking them?

I… no, I don’t think so. Not like my thoughts are being taken out or inserted, no. That sounds very specific, and I don’t think I’ve had that.

I mean, I can get worried that people can tell what I’m thinking from my face, if that makes sense. Like if I’m tense in a meeting or I’m trying very hard not to react to something, I’ll worry that it’s obvious, that everyone can see I’m uncomfortable or that I’m judging something or that I’m afraid. But that’s more like they can read my expression or my body language, not that they can literally hear the words in my head.

And I don’t feel like someone is putting thoughts into my mind. I have thoughts I don’t like, or thoughts that feel intrusive in the ordinary sense—like they pop up and I wish they wouldn’t—but they still feel like mine. Unwanted, maybe, but mine.

So… I guess the answer is no. I don’t have the experience of thoughts being removed, planted, or broadcast out loud to other people. At least not that I’ve noticed.

Have you ever felt that events, objects, or actions by others in your environment had a direct and special connection to you, even when there was no logical reason to believe so—like things were happening specifically because of you or to send you a message?

I’m not sure I’ve experienced it in that exact way. I mean, I can be very aware of what’s going on around me, and sometimes I’ll read into people’s behavior too much—like if someone sends a short email, or doesn’t make eye contact, or changes their tone, I might immediately start thinking, “Did I do something? Are they upset with me?” And because of my work, I’m used to looking for patterns and implications, so my mind can kind of run with things.

But feeling like an object or an event was specifically arranged for me, or that the universe or other people were sending me a message through ordinary things… I don’t think so. Not in a way where I truly believed it. I might have a passing thought like, “That’s strange timing,” or “That feels pointed,” especially if I’m already stressed, but then I usually recognize there could be other explanations.

So I guess I’d say no, not really. I may personalize things emotionally, and I can get caught up in trying to interpret people’s actions, but I don’t think I’ve had the feeling that random events or objects had a direct special connection to me without a logical reason.

Have you ever felt that certain things you see, hear, or experience in your daily life—like something on TV, a stranger’s action, or even a word in a book—were meant only for you, as if they were messages or signs specifically for you to understand?

I don’t think so… not in that “this was meant only for me” kind of way.

I do notice things, maybe more than I should. Like if I’m watching TV and something lines up with what I was already thinking about, I might feel a little startled, or if I read a word somewhere that happens to connect to something on my mind, I may pause and think, “That’s odd.” And sometimes I can stay with that feeling too long, like I keep turning it over and trying to decide whether it means anything.

But I don’t think I actually believe it’s a message for me. I don’t think a stranger doing something on the street is secretly signaling me, or that a book or a show is communicating with me personally. It’s more that I’m sensitive to coincidences and I can get anxious or overly focused on them, especially if I’m already under pressure.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve had that experience of things being signs meant specifically for me to understand. More like I notice patterns and then have to remind myself that noticing something doesn’t mean it was put there for me.

Have you ever felt that completely neutral or random things, like something written in a newspaper, a gesture from a stranger, or something happening on TV, were actually about you or had a hidden meaning that was only meant for you to understand?

I think that’s basically the same sort of thing you were asking before, right? And… no, I don’t think I can honestly say that happens to me in that way.

I mean, I notice coincidences. If the TV is on and someone says a word I was just thinking about, or I see an article headline that connects to something stressful in my life, I might sort of freeze for a second and think, “That’s weird.” And because I tend to analyze things, I can spend more time than I probably should wondering why it caught my attention.

But I don’t really feel like it’s about me, like the newspaper or the TV or some stranger is sending me a hidden message. I don’t have that sense that it was meant only for me to understand. It’s more like my mind grabs onto things when I’m already keyed up, and then I have to sort of talk myself back down and say, “Okay, that’s just a coincidence, or you’re just noticing it because it’s already on your mind.”

So no, not really. I can overread things emotionally, but I don’t think neutral random things are secretly about me.

Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by an outside force, like someone was putting thoughts into your mind or pulling them out, or that others could somehow hear your thoughts without you speaking them?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. I mean, I have times where my thoughts feel… overwhelming, or like they’re moving too fast, or I can’t get them to quiet down, especially if I’m stressed. But that’s different from feeling like someone else is literally putting them there.

I don’t think I’ve had the experience of an outside force controlling my thoughts, or pulling them out of my head. And I don’t think I’ve believed other people could actually hear what I was thinking without me saying it. I can worry about what people think of me, or imagine that they can tell I’m anxious just by looking at me, but that’s more like embarrassment or self-consciousness, not that they can hear the actual words in my mind.

So… no, I don’t think so. Not in that specific sense.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled, inserted, or removed by an outside force, or that someone else could hear your thoughts without you speaking them out loud?

I know you’re asking it again in a slightly different way, and I’m trying to answer it carefully, because I don’t want to overstate something just because my thoughts can feel intense sometimes.

I don’t really have a clear example of feeling like someone was inserting thoughts into my head or taking them out. That doesn’t sound quite right to me. My thoughts can feel like they’re racing or like I can’t get control of them, but they still feel like mine, if that makes sense. Unwanted, maybe, or too loud internally, but not like they came from a machine or a person outside me.

And with people hearing my thoughts… I can get very self-conscious, like I’ll think, “Can they tell what I’m thinking?” but I think I mean more from my face or my behavior, not literally hearing the words in my head. I don’t think I actually believe someone can hear them without me speaking.

So I guess my answer is no, not in that literal outside-force way. It’s more that my own mind can feel hard to manage sometimes.
